Compare component options that satisfy the same product specification.
Frame judgments around responsibilities for product functions, structures, materials, and architecture.
Includes design specifications and component trade-offs; assign production-batch control to process_engineering.
Compare process improvements that reduce interconnect manufacturing defects.
Frame judgments around manufacturing flows, process windows, yield, and scale-up responsibilities.
Includes production consistency; assign discussions limited to component function or structure to product_design.
Compare interface options between a sensor and a controller.
Frame judgments around interfaces, component coordination, and end-to-end system operation.
Includes hardware-software compatibility and system validation; assign the lifetime of a single component to reliability_engineering.
Compare connector-structure improvements for thermal-cycling failures.
Frame judgments around failure, service life, environmental tolerance, and repeatable operation.
Includes failure recovery and lifetime validation; assign purely scientific mechanism contributions to applied_research or scientific_contribution.
Plan a minimum validation for a new sampling architecture.
Frame judgments around the technical distinctions, prototypes, and disclosure evidence for an invention concept.
May apply to employed engineers; it does not imply independent-inventor status or patentability.
Study how noise mechanisms affect imaging performance.
Frame judgments around whether mechanisms, materials, or methods can explain and improve a specific application.
Focuses on translatable research evidence; do not infer employer type, and assign production-operations optimization to process_engineering.
Identify a testable gap in low-data reconstruction research.
Frame judgments around research gaps, testable questions, and contributions relative to prior work.
Do not infer an academic affiliation; assign work serving only product-function trade-offs to product_design.
Compare experimental methods for testing a mechanistic hypothesis.
Frame judgments around experimental design, measurement, benchmarks, and result reproducibility.
Includes comparisons of research methods; frame product acceptance planning from a product or reliability perspective.
Screen packaging technology paths suitable for a pilot.
Frame judgments around external technology supply, maturity, and adoption conditions.
Includes partnership candidates and pilot thresholds; assign customer positioning to product_strategy.
Compare initial use cases for launching a new detection platform.
Frame judgments around target customers, use cases, product positioning, and feature priorities.
Includes market-entry paths; assign external technology-supplier screening to technology_scouting.
Track the packaging R&D directions of different companies.
Frame judgments around competitor capabilities, technology changes, and relative positioning.
May use technology or patent evidence; the focus is comparison among organizations rather than parameter trade-offs for one solution.
Relate a product technology roadmap to patent-topic coverage.
Frame judgments around the coverage, positioning, and maintenance of technology assets against business roadmaps.
A specific portfolio analysis requires a defined asset scope; it is not an infringement assessment for a single product.
List the claim evidence needed to assess a design change.
Frame risk questions around product implementation, claims, legal status, and applicable scope.
General content may provide an evidence checklist; it must not treat search results as a definitive legal conclusion.
Organize the business inputs needed to determine ownership of collaborative R&D results.
Frame judgments around R&D collaboration, data use, ownership of results, and transaction responsibilities.
Requires an explicit collaboration or contract context; do not treat every Legal user as a patent attorney.
Design a reproducible patent-search strategy for microfluidic cartridges.
Frame judgments around search coverage, family dates, classifications, and feature-to-evidence mapping.
The focus is auditable evidence; the perspective does not imply professional representative status or legal advice.
Use a disclosure-support table to review draft claims.
Frame judgments around disclosure support, application documents, claims, and office-action responses.
When specific disclosure or prosecution materials are unavailable, generate a template only and do not invent application content.
Identify licensing candidates and missing validation evidence.
Frame judgments around matching technology assets with potential adopters, development gaps, and transaction readiness.
Requires an explicit licensing, transfer, or inbound-adoption context; do not infer an active transaction from the user's role.
Explain the different needs addressed by solution comparison and feasibility assessment.
Help compare possible tasks and deliverables when the task remains unclear.
Use only for task_clarification; it is not a catch-all tag for other well-defined tasks.
Medical Imaging Equipment & Diagnostic Imaging Software
Example topics: Detectors, imaging chains, reconstruction algorithms, and image interpretation workflows.
CT, MRI, ultrasound, and software that directly performs image reconstruction or supports diagnosis.
Hospital imaging services and general wellness applications are excluded; upstream detectors should also be associated with the Electronics industry.
Example topics: Sample preparation, reagent systems, microfluidic cartridges, and signal detection.
Clinical diagnostic reagents, instruments, molecular diagnostic systems, and at-home testing products.
Research-use reagents belong to H13 Life Science Research Tools; hospital laboratory services are not medical-device manufacturing.
Example topics: Electrochemical sensors, skin interfaces, micropumps, and control and alert pathways.
Continuous glucose monitors, blood glucose meters, insulin pumps, and related closed-loop devices.
Insulin drugs belong to Pharmaceuticals; nonmedical fitness wearables and general wellness software are excluded.
Surgical Robotics & Minimally Invasive Surgical Systems
Example topics: Robotic arms, flexible catheters, wristed instruments, visual navigation, and operator interfaces.
Surgical robots, endoscopic and interventional platforms, specialized instruments, and intraoperative navigation.
General-purpose industrial robots belong to Industrial Automation; hospital surgical services are excluded.
Example topics: Glass-fiber-reinforced thermoplastics, carbon-fiber composites, and low-loss polymers.
Modified resins, engineering plastics, fiber-reinforced composites, and semi-finished materials; select this segment when the primary business is material supply.
Coating and adhesive formulations belong to M10; finished automotive or electronic products belong to their respective end-use industries.
Example topics: Nickel-based alloys, titanium alloys, and metal powders for additive manufacturing.
R&D and supply of nickel-based superalloys, titanium alloys, specialty steels, and metal powders.
Commodity steel trading is not treated as a priority topic; finished aerospace or medical components belong to their end-use industries.
Example topics: Boron nitride fillers, low-dielectric glass, and technical ceramic substrates.
Electrically insulating and thermally conductive ceramics, ceramic fibers, fused silica, and functional glass.
Construction cement belongs to M14; decorative ceramics and ordinary household glass are outside the current scope.
Example topics: LFP cathodes, silicon-based anodes, electrolytes, and recycled materials.
Cathode and anode active materials, electrolytes, separator materials, and recycled or regenerated materials.
Cells, battery packs, and energy-storage systems belong to M05; mining is treated only as an upstream tag.
Example topics: Traction motors, inverters, transmissions, and electric-drive thermal management.
Motors, inverters, electric drive axles, and hybrid coupling systems for BEVs, HEVs, and PHEVs.
Battery-cell materials and standalone storage batteries belong to Energy or Materials; chassis and automated-driving systems are separate segments.
Example topics: Fusion of vehicle cameras and radar, decision stacks, scenarios, and safety evidence.
Perception fusion, driving decisions, control, safety validation, and in-vehicle computing integration.
General-purpose sensor chips belong to Semiconductors; driver-assistance systems must not be treated as equivalent to fully autonomous driving.
Example topics: Body joining, braking and suspension components, and thermal-management assemblies.
Braking, steering, suspension, body structures, cabins, and automotive thermal-management components.
Electric powertrains and ADAS algorithms are separate segments; raw materials belong to the Materials industry.
Example topics: Vehicle architectures, body-equipment interfaces, power systems, and duty cycles.
Vehicle and systems engineering for road trucks, buses, commercial vans, and special-purpose vehicles.
Passenger vehicles and fleet-operation services are excluded; off-road construction and agricultural machinery belong to their respective machinery industries.
Example topics: Chip architectures, interconnect packaging, wafer processes, and device reliability.
Chip design, wafer fabrication, packaging, and testing across logic, memory, analog, and power devices.
Finished systems, PCBs, and standalone optical instruments are excluded; semiconductor equipment should be classified by its primary equipment-manufacturing activity.
Example topics: Multilayer boards, microvias, solder joints, connector contacts, and passive networks.
PCBs, connectors, passive components, and electronic assembly interconnects, including rigid-flex boards.
Semiconductor chips, complete server systems, and complete optical systems are excluded.
Example topics: Server nodes, switches, rack interconnects, and hardware cooling.
Hardware and systems integration for servers, storage systems, network switching, and communications equipment.
Pure-software SaaS, chip design, and data-center power infrastructure are excluded.
Example topics: Laser sources, optical paths, imaging or spectroscopic sensing, and calibration chains.
Lasers, optical instruments, imaging and spectroscopic detection systems, and optical sensing modules.
Chip-level semiconductor devices belong to E01; non-optical sensors should be classified by their actual end-use industry.
Example topics: Robot bodies, end effectors, vision systems, and work-cell control.
Industrial robots, collaborative robots, machine-vision integration, and automated work cells.
Consumer robots are excluded; standalone non-robotic processing equipment belongs to a separate segment.
Example topics: Spindles, motion axes, cutting tools, and process control.
Metalworking machine tools, forming equipment, and specialized production equipment; add customer-specific tags for relevant machinery subdomains.
Robotics and additive-manufacturing equipment are separate segments; civil construction services are excluded.
Example topics: Printing equipment, powder spreading or energy input, in-process monitoring, and build processes.
Industrial 3D printers, process monitoring, control systems, and equipment integration.
Printing powders and resins belong to Materials; pure printing services should receive additional tags based on the customer's end-use industry.
Example topics: Facility or system concepts, computational models, interfaces, and engineering deliverables.
Engineering analysis, design, technical consulting, and integration recommendations for facilities, systems, and products.
Equipment manufacturing, construction contracting, general management consulting, and legal services are excluded.
Example topics: Antibody sequences, binding structures, linkers and payloads, formulations, and analytical methods.
Monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and other therapeutic proteins.
Small-molecule drugs are excluded; contract manufacturing belongs to CDMO; cell and gene therapies are separate segments.
Example topics: Cell populations, vectors, editing systems, delivery, and potency assays.
Cell therapies such as CAR-T, in vivo and ex vivo gene therapies, and gene-editing therapies.
Gene editing for nontherapeutic uses belongs to the relevant agricultural or industrial segment; general reagents and pure CDMO services are separate segments.
Example topics: Cell lines, culture media, bioreactors, purification, and formulation processes.
Biologics CDMO, cell-line development, culture and purification, analytical testing, and technology-transfer services.
Proprietary drug discovery belongs to the relevant medicines segment; general equipment sales may also be associated with Engineering.
Example topics: Enzyme sequences, production strains, fermentation processes, enzyme formulations, and application processes.
Enzymes, production microorganisms, and related formulations for cleaning, textiles, papermaking, and industrial bioprocessing.
Food ingredients belong to the Food segment; finished renewable fuels belong to Chemical, with Energy used as an application tag; finished polymers belong to Materials.
Life Science Research Tools & Laboratory Instruments
Example topics: Sequencing and imaging platforms, microfluidics, reagent chemistry, sample preparation, and analytical workflows.
Research-use sequencing, single-cell and multi-omics instruments, sample preparation, analytical reagents, and laboratory automation.
Integrated IVD products for clinical diagnosis belong to H02; biologics CDMO belongs to H07; research use does not imply approval for clinical use.
Example topics: Agricultural-machine actuators, positioning and visual perception, operation control, and prescription maps.
Autonomous-guidance farm machinery, precision seeding, variable-rate application, sensing, and agricultural-operation systems.
Businesses primarily focused on engineering and manufacturing may also be associated with Engineering; crop-production services are not equipment R&D.
Example topics: Germplasm, molecular markers, breeding processes, crop traits, and field phenotyping.
Commercial seeds, seedlings, and crop-trait development through conventional and biotechnology-assisted breeding.
Agricultural machinery belongs to the agricultural-equipment segment; pesticides and biological-control products are not separate segments in this version and may be supplemented with Other.
Example topics: Food matrices, microbial control, heat and mass transfer, and freezing or drying processes.
Manufacturing of frozen fruit and vegetables, frozen meals, and ready-to-eat convenience foods, with emphasis on processing and preservation.
Dedicated food-machinery manufacturing may also be associated with Engineering; raw grains, beverages, and cold-chain transportation services are excluded.
Example topics: Protein fractions, dietary fibers, fermentation cultures, food enzymes, and emulsification or gel systems.
Proteins, dietary fibers, enzymes, microbial cultures, functional ingredients, and application formulations for food manufacturing.
Therapeutic drugs belong to Biopharmaceuticals; industrial-use enzymes belong to Industrial Biotechnology; alternative protein does not represent the entire segment.
Example topics: Battery cells, storage battery clusters, battery-management systems, and storage power-conversion systems.
Battery-cell manufacturing, battery packs, battery-management systems, power-conversion systems, and commercial, industrial, or grid-scale storage integration.
Active materials belong to M04; vehicle powertrains belong to Automotive; this segment does not encompass power generation in general.
Example topics: Distribution transformers, switchgear cabinets, protection relays, and dynamic line-rating monitoring.
Transformers, switchgear, cables, protection and control systems, and grid-enhancement technologies.
Generation equipment belongs to its corresponding industry; electricity trading alone does not fit this R&D profile.
Example topics: Photovoltaic cells, encapsulated modules, tracking structures, and inverters.
R&D and manufacturing of photovoltaic cells and modules, encapsulation, tracking structures, and inverters.
General wafer-level semiconductors belong to Electronics; upstream resins and glass belong to Materials.
Example topics: PEM and alkaline electrolyzers, fuel-cell membrane-electrode assemblies, and balance-of-plant systems.
Electrolyzers, fuel-cell stacks, hydrogen compression and transport or storage equipment, and balance-of-plant systems.
Commodity industrial hydrogen supply belongs to M11; hydrogen-derived fuel synthesis belongs to M12.
Example topics: Photoresists, CMP slurries, electronic-grade cleaning solutions, and electroplating additives.
Photoresists, wet electronic chemicals, CMP slurries, electroplating additives, and deposition precursors.
Commodity industrial gases belong to M11; wafer-device and packaging services belong to Electronics.
Example topics: Waterborne coatings, structural adhesives, thermally conductive adhesives, and weather-resistant sealants.
R&D and manufacturing of industrial and functional coatings, structural adhesives, electronic adhesives, and construction sealants.
Base-resin supply belongs to M01; application and installation businesses should receive an additional service-activity tag.
Example topics: Ultra-high-purity nitrogen and argon, electronic specialty gases, purifiers, and gas-supply systems.
High-purity and specialty gases, air separation, purification, gas distribution, and recovery supply systems.
Hydrogen-energy equipment belongs to M08; catalysts should not be combined with gases as a single segment.
Example topics: HEFA and alcohol-to-jet processes, catalysts, and renewable feedstocks.
Chemical-conversion production of sustainable aviation fuel, renewable diesel, bio-alcohols, and synthetic fuels.
Fermentation-platform R&D belongs to Biotechnology with a cross-industry tag; hydrogen-production equipment belongs to M08.
Example topics: Heat-pump compressors, heat exchangers, refrigerant circuits, and building controls.
R&D and manufacturing of heat pumps, air-conditioning and ventilation systems, water-heating equipment, and building controls.
Construction and installation should receive an additional contractor or service tag; equipment manufacturers must not be treated as building contractors.
Example topics: Low-clinker binder systems, supplementary cementitious materials, and concrete mix designs.
Cement, binders, ready-mixed and precast concrete, with low-carbon technologies represented through tags.
The primary activity is building-material supply or product R&D; on-site concrete contracting should receive a separate activity tag; this segment does not encompass all materials.
Example topics: Building modules, wall panels, structural connectors, and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing interfaces.
Factory-produced modules and panel systems, structural connections, and integrated mechanical, electrical, and plumbing delivery.
Distinguish factory manufacturing, design, and on-site installation as separate activities; this segment is not equivalent to property development or the entire construction industry.
Example topics: Membrane treatment, adsorption media, aeration systems, and water-supply and drainage networks.
Water-supply and drainage networks, treatment processes and equipment, water reuse, and infrastructure-renewal projects.
Water-utility operations, engineering construction, and equipment R&D should receive separate activity tags; this segment does not encompass the entire environmental industry.
Example topics: Aircraft structures, propulsion or avionics, satellite systems, and their environmental qualification.

Aircraft, aviation propulsion and avionics, satellites, and spacecraft components or systems; add this as a named industry under Other, and migrate legacy Engineering users based on their target product or system.
Airline operations and tourism services are excluded; land and naval defense systems and pure cybersecurity are excluded.
Example: keep the question at the overall industry level without selecting a segment.
Use null when scope_level is industry.
A non-null segment is required when scope_level is industry_segment.
Example task: Find adoptable technical solutions for a specified function or problem.
Find adoptable technical solutions for a specified function or problem.
Do not substitute a broad field survey for a problem-driven search.
Example task: Compare identified approaches or solutions under shared constraints and evaluation criteria.
Compare identified approaches or solutions under shared constraints and evaluation criteria.
This is distinct from finding solutions; use research_method_comparison for comparisons limited to research methods.
Example task: Start from a defined failure mode or performance failure to identify corrective actions and validation.
Start from a defined failure mode or performance failure to identify corrective actions and validation.
The goal is to restore function; use evidence_synthesis when the goal is only to explain a scientific mechanism.
Example task: Adjust manufacturing or operating parameters and workflows to improve yield, consistency, or efficiency.
Adjust manufacturing or operating parameters and workflows to improve yield, consistency, or efficiency.
Exclude work that changes only product positioning or a research question.
Example task: Organize evidence on existing approaches, technology categories, and maturity.
Organize evidence on existing approaches, technology categories, and maturity.
Focuses on a static structure; use technology_trend_tracking for monitoring change over time.
Example task: Turn user problems and technical capabilities into a testable product or invention concept.
Turn user problems and technical capabilities into a testable product or invention concept.
Use research_ideation for questions about scientific contribution.
Example task: Determine whether a solution has sufficient basis for implementation under specified conditions and identify evidence gaps.
Determine whether a solution has sufficient basis for implementation under specified conditions and identify evidence gaps.
When conditions are missing, state conditional judgments; use validation_planning to design the validation work.
Example task: Design an experiment, prototype, or test path for evaluating a hypothesis or solution.
Design an experiment, prototype, or test path for evaluating a hypothesis or solution.
Do not claim that experiments have been completed; use research_method_search when the task is to find a research method.
Example task: Map the core questions, research paths, and foundational knowledge needed to enter a new field.
Map the core questions, research paths, and foundational knowledge needed to enter a new field.
Do not replace the problem structure with a popularity ranking.
Example task: Use existing evidence and limitations to identify unresolved, researchable questions.
Use existing evidence and limitations to identify unresolved, researchable questions.
Failure to retrieve evidence does not prove absence; use research_ideation to formulate a specific research project.
Example task: Find measurement, experimental, or analytical methods for a research question.
Find measurement, experimental, or analytical methods for a research question.
Do not treat a product-manufacturing process as a research method without justification.
Example task: Compare the assumptions, sample requirements, applicability, and limitations of research methods.
Compare the assumptions, sample requirements, applicability, and limitations of research methods.
Use solution_comparison for product technology paths.
Example task: Turn research gaps into hypotheses, research topics, and testable paths.
Turn research gaps into hypotheses, research topics, and testable paths.
Do not merely list broad research directions; use product_ideation for concepts driven by product needs.
Example task: Build an auditable source set around a defined topic and explain relevance.
Build an auditable source set around a defined topic and explain relevance.
Use specialized tasks for prior-art or FTO searches; state the source types in the search scope.
Example task: Explain common findings, disagreements, and applicability limits across multiple studies.
Explain common findings, disagreements, and applicability limits across multiple studies.
Do not treat patent publications as experimental validation; use evidence_search for a search-results list.
Example task: Observe changes over time in scientific questions, research methods, or findings.
Observe changes over time in scientific questions, research methods, or findings.
Use technology_trend_tracking when commercialization and industry adoption are the main focus.
Example task: Track technology paths, performance advances, and adoption evidence over time.
Track technology paths, performance advances, and adoption evidence over time.
Use technology_landscape for a static inventory and research_trend_tracking for purely academic evolution.
Example task: Track changes in the capabilities, R&D, and products of specified organizations or organization types.
Track changes in the capabilities, R&D, and products of specified organizations or organization types.
When no organizations are provided, explain the screening method rather than inventing the user's competitors.
Example task: Screen opportunities from unmet needs, technical capabilities, and application gaps.
Screen opportunities from unmet needs, technical capabilities, and application gaps.
Use licensing_opportunity_assessment when a specific licensing transaction is the goal.
Example task: Weigh R&D directions by value, evidence, maturity, and resource requirements.
Weigh R&D directions by value, evidence, maturity, and resource requirements.
Do not invent actual company scores when resource constraints and budgets are unavailable.
Example task: Organize patent-positioning evidence by topic, organization, time, and family.
Organize patent-positioning evidence by topic, organization, time, and family.
A patent landscape is not product FTO; use ip_portfolio_planning for decisions about owned assets.
Example task: Locate relevant earlier public evidence for defined technical features and a stated search purpose.
Locate relevant earlier public evidence for defined technical features and a stated search purpose.
State the search date range; do not automatically draw a novelty conclusion.
Example task: Compare specified technical features item by item with earlier evidence and identify gaps.
Compare specified technical features item by item with earlier evidence and identify gaps.
A technical distinction is not a patentability conclusion; provide a comparison method when disclosure is missing.
Example task: Collect claims and legal-status signals around a product implementation, target scope, and time frame.
Collect claims and legal-status signals around a product implementation, target scope, and time frame.
This differs from a prior-art search; when scope is missing, provide a search framework without declaring clearance.
Example task: Compare a design implementation or change with relevant claim evidence and identify issues requiring review.
Compare a design implementation or change with relevant claim evidence and identify issues requiring review.
Design-around assumptions require validation; when scope is missing, limit the output to a method and risk checklist.
Example task: Organize evidence gaps and action items related to technology use, patents, or ownership.
Organize evidence gaps and action items related to technology use, patents, or ownership.
Do not automatically expand into contract negotiation or definitive legal advice; use collaboration_terms_review for a specific contract.
Example task: Organize patent-application documents and their support relationships from a technical disclosure.
Organize patent-application documents and their support relationships from a technical disclosure.
Do not invent technical features; provide a template when only the three profile inputs are available.
Example task: Review a supplied document for technical support, wording consistency, and required revisions.
Review a supplied document for technical support, wording consistency, and required revisions.
A document to review is required; otherwise provide a review template.
Example task: Organize core features and a claim hierarchy from a technical disclosure.
Organize core features and a claim hierarchy from a technical disclosure.
Do not invent invention features from an industry name; use a template when disclosure is unavailable.
Example task: Recommend scope, dependency, and wording changes to existing claims and supporting materials.
Recommend scope, dependency, and wording changes to existing claims and supporting materials.
Provide only a template when the original claims and supporting materials are unavailable.
Example task: Map supplied objections and cited references to the application's supporting materials and identify response issues.
Map supplied objections and cited references to the application's supporting materials and identify response issues.
Do not infer office-action content or deadlines from an industry; use a template when materials are missing.
Example task: Organize a response and amendment support from a supplied office action and application materials.
Organize a response and amendment support from a supplied office action and application materials.
Provide only a response-structure template when specific materials are missing.
Example task: Relate technology assets, application evidence, and adopter needs to identify transaction-readiness gaps.
Relate technology assets, application evidence, and adopter needs to identify transaction-readiness gaps.
Requires a licensing, transfer, or inbound-adoption context; do not invent expressions of partner interest.
Example task: Map collaboration goals, results, and data use to contractual business issues that require discussion.
Map collaboration goals, results, and data use to contractual business issues that require discussion.

Example task: Plan technology-asset coverage, business priorities, and maintenance directions.
Plan technology-asset coverage, business priorities, and maintenance directions.
A specific plan requires an asset scope; otherwise provide only a planning-method template.
Example task: Help distinguish among tasks, required materials, and corresponding deliverables.
Help distinguish among tasks, required materials, and corresponding deliverables.
Do not use it in place of an already well-defined task.

List candidates, screening criteria, and applicable conditions.
Do more than list names; prefer comparison_matrix when candidates can be compared on a common basis.
Example deliverable: Compare multiple options using consistent metrics, conditions, and evidence standards.
Compare multiple options using consistent metrics, conditions, and evidence standards.

Example deliverable: Organize field coverage and relationships by topic, technology path, or organization.
Organize field coverage and relationships by topic, technology path, or organization.

Describe the problem, the concept's distinctions, its rationale, and minimum validation.

Organize conditions, evidence, gaps, and the basis for further judgment on a defined question.

Specify the hypothesis, samples or operating conditions, methods, metrics, and decision rules.

Present research gaps, specific questions, rationale, and testable paths.

Map sources and locations to supported technical features or conclusions.

Synthesize multiple sources, disagreements, and limitations.

Describe changes, evidence, and implications within a defined time window.

Prioritize candidates against objectives, evaluation dimensions, and evidence.

Identify issues, rationale, and recommended revisions item by item in an existing document.

Organize a claim hierarchy and supporting basis from a defined technical disclosure.

Organize a response structure and supporting evidence from a supplied office action and application materials.
Use document_template when the specific office action and related documents are unavailable.
Example deliverable: Relate technology assets, adopter needs, development gaps, and transaction readiness.
Relate technology assets, adopter needs, development gaps, and transaction readiness.
